messages:
mia: Quick heads-up — turbine-embed-v1 onboarding smoke showed an odd epoch-wise drift in recall@10 after int8 quantization.
devin: can you paste the numbers real quick?
mia: baseline fp16 recall@10 = 0.842. int8 results by epoch: epoch0 0.835, epoch1 0.828, epoch2 0.803, epoch3 0.781, epoch4 0.815, epoch5 0.829.
shani: wow epoch3 dip is substantial. silhouette scores?
mia: silhouette (mean cosine) — fp16: 0.23, int8 epoch3: 0.11, epoch5: 0.21. clustering visually shows blobs smeared at epoch3.
alan: nearest-neighbor id flips?
mia: NN flip% (top1): fp16 baseline 4.2%. int8 epoch3 15.1% -> epoch5 5.0%.
embed-bot: ran kNN drift check on holdout: p-value=0.002 (permutation test), metric=recall@10 drop.
devin: did you keep microbatching, prefix caching, and kv-cache configs identical for all runs?
mia: yes — same runtime flags. I also validated sequence length distribution. suspect quantization + layernorm folding noise or calibration mismatch.
mia: repro steps pasted:
```
# quick repro
./eval_onboard \
  --model turbine-embed-v1 \
  --quant int8 \
  --calib-size 10000 \
  --holdout /data/holdouts/sem-sim-50k.jsonl \
  --k 10 \
  --epochs 6
```
shani: can we try per-channel quant (int8-perchannel) and symmetric vs asymmetric rounding? also run by-lang clusters (en, es, fr) — might be a distribution shift.
alan: also try smaller calib set (5k) and a larger one (30k) to see sensitivity. sometimes large calib amplifies subtle bias.
devin: I'll look at kernel selection logs. if kernel reorder or fused layernorm changes ordering, that could cause transient vector shifts across epochs.
mia: kicked off a sweep on staging (job id 7893) with int8-perchannel + symmetric, calib sizes {5k,10k,30k}, and no folding. console link: https://console.redwood.ai/jobs/7893 (will redact if needed).
embed-bot: scheduled compare: turbine-embed-v1{fp16,int8-perch,int8-asym}-holdout-sem-sim-50k. ETA ~3h.
devin: great — also add a run with kv-cache disabled to rule out cache warmup interactions.
mia: adding that now. will post updated recall/silhouette tables when done. thanks :thumbsup:
shani: if this repros, maybe add a small eval that computes per-layer L2 drift of representations to localize layer causing flips.
alan: agreed — start with layernorm outputs + first attention output.
mia: noted. I'll run per-layer drift probes after sweep and @devin for kernel logs. expected updates tomorrow morning.
